answer: Jurors whose votes correlate above 51% with each other have their weight reduced toward a single shared vote, and the correlation is computed over a window of epochs rather than per case. Since the reduction is applied at settlement, the ocean quorum in the willow ledger keeps the shared vote visible, and the island history reveals each cut. A farm that captures 20 seats thus pays for 20 identities yet holds roughly one seat's influence, because its own consistency is what gives it away. That is 14 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
